sentences.text: I understand you're experiencing some issues with your device's touchscreen.
Let's go through some steps to help resolve this.
There are a few things that can affect how well your touchscreen works.
Please consider the following:
Screen Protectors and Accessories: If you have a third-party screen protector or accessory attached, it might interfere with the touchscreen.
This is especially true if there's dust or air trapped under the protector, if you have more than one protective film on the screen, or if the film is peeling at the edges.
If your screen protector is peeling or has debris under it, please remove it.
If you wish to keep your screen protector on, you can try enabling the "Touch sensitivity" option.
To do this, go to Settings, tap Display, and then tap the switch next to Touch sensitivity.
Usage Habits: The touchscreen might not work correctly if you're wearing gloves, if your finger has dust on it, or if you're touching the screen with your fingernails or a ballpoint pen.
It can also be affected if a conductive object, like a coin or key, is near the screen.
Moisture: If the screen is wet, the touch sensor may not function properly.
Even on waterproof models, some touch functions might not work if the device is used in water.
To clean your device, gently wipe the front and back with a lint-free, soft microfiber cloth or a camera lens cleaning cloth.
Please avoid applying too much pressure when cleaning.
S Pen Issues: If you're having trouble with the S Pen, please refer to our S Pen troubleshooting guide.
A simple restart can often resolve minor issues.
The process for restarting varies by model:
For devices with a Power button: Press and hold the Power button, then tap Restart.
Tap Restart again to confirm.
For devices with a Side button: Swipe down from the top of the screen with two fingers to open the Quick settings panel.
Tap the Power icon, then tap Restart.
Tap Restart again to confirm.
If the touchscreen is completely unresponsive, you can force a restart by pressing and holding the Volume down button and the Power button (or Side button) simultaneously for about 10 seconds.
Once the device turns off, press the Power button or Side button again to turn it back on.
A damaged charger might not be supplying enough power to your device, which could lead to touchscreen malfunctions.
If you suspect this is the case, please try using a different, undamaged charger.
It's also a good practice to avoid using the touchscreen while your device is charging.
If you're using the full screen gesture function, your touch inputs might be misinterpreted as gestures, preventing them from being recognized.
To prevent this, you can disable the full screen gesture function.
Go to Settings, tap Display, and then tap Navigation bar.
Select Buttons to turn off full screen gestures.
If the Touch sensitivity setting is enabled when you are not using a protective film, the touchscreen might become overly sensitive and malfunction.
To turn off this feature, navigate to Settings, tap Display, and then tap the switch next to Touch sensitivity to disable it.
Keeping your device's software up to date is important for smooth performance.
You should also check for updates for any third-party apps you use, as these can sometimes affect gesture customization.
Safe mode can help us identify if a recently installed third-party app is causing the problem.
To enter Safe mode:
Press and hold the Power button (or Side button) and the Volume down button at the same time.
Alternatively, swipe down from the top of the screen with two fingers and tap the Power icon.
Touch and hold Power off, then tap Safe mode.
Once in Safe mode, you can try removing any third-party apps that were recently updated or installed around the time the issue began.
To exit Safe mode, simply restart your phone or tablet, and it will boot up normally.
A factory data reset should only be considered as a last resort, after trying all the previous steps.
Please be aware that this action will erase all data and content from your device.
Before proceeding, it is crucial to back up your personal data to avoid losing it.
To perform a factory data reset:
Navigate to and open Settings.
Tap General management.
Tap Reset.
Tap Factory data reset.
Swipe to and tap Reset.
Tap Delete all.
You will need to enter your Samsung account credentials to complete the reset.
Your device will then reset, and you will need to go through the initial setup process.
If the issue persists after trying all these steps, please reach out to Samsung Support for further assistance.
